description: Handheld T Display P4 & ESP32-P4 SDR scanners - RTL-SDR or LR2021 SDR, P25 Phase 1, FM/AM, ADS-B and POCSAG, plus onboard LoRa/MeshCore, GPS and Flipper .sub capture. No PC.

latest_release.name: LakeShark 3.1.0 (T-Display P4)
latest_release.body:
Update over Wi-Fi from UPDATE, or install `lakeshark-tdp4-3.1.0.zip` with the web flasher on terminalbay.com. LakeShark Desktop, Studio and the ESP32-P4-NANO stay on 2.22.0.

New:

- WARDRIVE REPLAY: play back any saved drive (R, or OPTIONS > REPLAY A DRIVE) from 1x to 32x, with pause and a seek bar. A three hour drive opens in about 11 seconds.
- WARDRIVE 3D: your drive over the real map, with place names. Turn, tilt and zoom with the keys or drag to pan; FOLLOW stays on the board, CHASE rides behind it, and FIT ALL shows the whole drive. Tap a marker for the network's card and every place it was seen. Zoomed out, finds gather into labelled columns.
- WARDRIVE 3D: HIDE gives the whole screen to the view, and LIGHT MAP switches to a light map. Speed, heading and counts sit on top, and the route is coloured by finds per minute.
- Card apps can use a USB SDR (RTL-SDR or HackRF) and the board's radio at the same time, for BUGHUNT's DUAL hunt.

Better:

- MAP always opens: when memory is short it starts with a lighter map, makes room, and returns to full detail by itself.
- MAP keeps your downloaded map while a pan crosses a coast or the edge of the downloaded area.
- MAP draws zoomed-out views much faster, and far out it keeps them readable: big rivers and main roads, with place names spread across the picture.
- WARDRIVE: the LIST scrolls with a finger, and MAP LAYER shows your drive on the map.
- The boot globe turns smoothly the whole time, with city lights on the night side.
- HOME: the WIFI/BT KIT folder sits in FIELD beside WARDRIVE, and BOOT LOG and MESH LANGUAGES are in SYSTEM.

Better on LR2021 boards:

- RTL-SDR and HackRF dongles work on LR2021 boards with the one firmware.
- LR2021 modules without a TCXO keep their crystal setting, and a learned frequency correction can be set from another board's packets.
- LoRa hears nodes that sit off frequency: up to a third of the channel width either side (41 kHz at 125 kHz), up from about 31 kHz. Nodes on modules without a TCXO now decode.
- LoRa takes the narrow bandwidths 7.8, 10.4, 15.6 and 20.8 kHz, and a long packet at those bandwidths is allowed the time it needs to send.
- DIAG shows the LR2021's own temperature and supply voltage.
- LoRa packet details show each packet's own coding rate.
- The radio checks every answer before using it, and front-end calibration tries again when a strong nearby signal interrupts it.

From 3.0.2:

Fixed:

- MAP: panning stays on one map. The detailed map and the world tiles no longer swap back and forth while you drag, place names stay put, and the picture no longer redraws after it settles.
- MAP: the edge a pan uncovers fills in with detail directly, without a rough outline first.
- MAP: map files and cells count only where the card's map can draw them, so an old download no longer sends MAP to a blank picture.
- MAP: zoom out all the way to the whole world from a downloaded map; the world map takes over where the download stops.
- Chat and file locker downloads have a size and time limit.

From 3.0.1:

Fixed:

- PACKS: drag the list with a finger to scroll it, and drag the globe to turn it to any place in the world. The new + and - keys on the globe zoom in and out.
- STORE: the list stays where your finger scrolls it.

From 3.0.0:

One firmware for every T-Display P4: the board finds its radio (SX1262 or LR2021) and its screen at boot. TFT boards keep their own image until one has been tested on this one.

New:

- FREQS by location: a frequency database built from public data (FCC licences for P25, DMR, NXDN and public-safety FM, airports, NOAA weather radio, marine channels). Pick the areas you want in PACKS and install them over Wi-Fi, from terminalbay.com, or by copying to the card. In the field, GPS picks among the packs you installed, with no network. Installed packs update themselves on Wi-Fi.
- GPS is on from the first boot, and apps that care about where you are use it.
- World maps: line maps of the whole world in the style o

detail.readme:
A radio lab that fits in your hand

P25 voice · FM · Aircraft · Pagers · MeshCore · Wardriving · Wi-Fi and Bluetooth tools

Open-source firmware for the LILYGO T-Display P4.
Install it from your browser in a minute, then it updates itself over Wi-Fi.

Install LakeShark  ·  See it in action  ·  Documentation

No dongle needed

On LR2021 boards the LoRa chip is the radio. P25 voice, aircraft, FM and pagers with nothing plugged in, plus live waterfalls, raw I/Q capture and programs that run on the chip's own CPU.

The on-chip programs build on Alex Beal's lr2021-re: his FFT, sweep and LoRa scanner, and the ARC toolchain and Patch RAM loader. Read his write-up · Explore LR2021-SDR

Install from Chrome or Edge with the browser installer. After that, the UPDATE app updates over Wi-Fi.

Power: use the P4's own USB-C port, not the keyboard's 5V output, or it keeps restarting.

LakeShark Desktop and Studio

Run every app in windows on your PC. Write your own in minutes.

Make your first app →

Real hardware, not an emulator (but also an emulator too). The apps run on a Waveshare ESP32-P4-NANO-DB with its radios and SD card. Your PC is its screen, mouse and keyboard over one USB cable.

Run every app in its own window on your PC, or press Ctrl+F11 to give one app the whole screen at twice the frame rate. Write your own apps in Studio, test them in the simulator and put them on the board, or do the same from a terminal with lsdk. The app store installs anything in one click.

Get Desktop 2.22.0  ·  Make your first app

What's New

3.1: WARDRIVE replays your drives in 3D over the real map · MAP always opens and draws far out faster · LR2021 hears off-frequency LoRa nodes

3.0: One firmware for every T-Display P4 · FREQS by location · World maps · App store on the board · LOCKER and CHAT · Lock screen

2.20: LR2021 on-chip programs · LakeShark Desktop · App SDK and Studio

3.1.0 release notes  ·  All releases

Meet the LakeShark

LILYGO T-Display P4 · 4.1" AMOLED · ESP32-P4 · LR2021 or SX1262
Touchscreen, GPS, motion sensing, and an optional detachable MIX-RF keyboard.

More screenshots

## Applications About thirty built in: P25 voice and trunking, FM with pagers, ADS-B, waterfalls, MeshCore, Sub-GHz capture and replay, FT8, wardriving, world maps, compass, GPS and music. More in the [app store](https://terminalbay.com/?m=lakeshark-apps), including community apps. Each one has a guide in the [wiki](https://terminalbay.com/?m=wiki#tdp4/APPS). The [web tools](https://terminalbay.com/?m=lakeshark) make P25 profiles, GPS scan lists, channel memories and map tiles. See also [replay and aircraft details](docs/REPLAY_AND_AIRCRAFT.md). ### Headless The **Waveshare ESP32-P4-NANO** and **ESP32-P4-WIFI6** run the same receivers without a screen. Control them from a serial console, a Flipper Zero or the [remote terminal](#remote-terminal). On the NANO the terminal is the full interface; `panel term 160x40` sets its size. The [LakeShark-Flipper app](https://github.com/SAMS0N1TE/LakeShark-Flipper) uses a Flipper Zero as the screen and buttons. It connects over Bluetooth (no pairing code) or GPIO.
Offline aircraft map ADS-B traffic
App launcher P25 radio

Flipper setup guide →

## Experimental features
Feature Status
P25 Phase II Grant following, bench-tested with public recordings; live RF unverified. Off after restart. Details
HackRF One FM, POCSAG, ACARS, P25, recording and ADS-B. Pagers verified; live P25 unconfirmed. Status
LR2021 I/Q TX Short custom waveforms, including P25 test tones and temperature packets. Research
LR2021 I/Q replay 433 MHz captures. OOK replay verified; FSK not yet verified over the air
C6 firmware update From the SD card. Recovery still needs the UART header. Details
Wi-Fi terminal Telnet on 2323 with a password. SSH on 22 on ESP32-P4-NANO builds. USB is the tested link
LoRa bearing plots RSSI by compass heading. Not validated direction finding
Location scanning Mixed P25/FM lists, GPS filtering and CSV/JSON import. Details
RadioReference adapter Needs an approved API key and Premium account. Live sign-in unverified

## Build from source ESP-IDF **5.5.4** with the six fixes in `bench/patches/`, applied once: ```powershell pwsh -File bench/patch-idf.ps1 -IdfPath /path/to/esp-idf -Apply ``` One build directory per target: ```sh # T-Display P4, every edition: the release image (radio and screen found at boot) idf.py -B build_tdp4_u -D SDKCONFIG=build_tdp4_u/sdkconfig -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;boards/t_display_p4.defaults;boards/t_display_p4_universal.defaults" build # T-Display P4 AMOLED only (568 × 1232, 16 MB) idf.py -B build_tdp4 -D SDKCONFIG=build_tdp4/sdkconfig -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;boards/t_display_p4.defaults" build # T-Display P4 TFT only (HI8561, 540 × 1168) idf.py -B build_tdp4_tft -D SDKCONFIG=build_tdp4_tft/sdkconfig -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;boards/t_display_p4.defaults;boards/t_display_p4_tft.defaults" build # LakeShark LR: LR2021 only, no USB host, RTL-SDR, HackRF or SX1262 idf.py -B build_tdp4_lr -D SDKCONFIG=build_tdp4_lr/sdkconfig -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;boards/t_display_p4.defaults;boards/t_display_p4_lr2021.defaults" build # Waveshare P4 headless idf.py -B build_nano -D SDKCONFIG=build_nano/sdkconfig -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;boards/nano_headless_ble.defaults" build ``` `boards/` holds the target defaults and partition layouts; `main/idf_component.yml` pins dependencies. Host checks: `pwsh -File bench/verify.ps1 -Level host`

## Contributors
@zenobik T-Display P4 TFT support (#8), UTF-8 text shown as ASCII letters (#9), LR2021 frequency correction for modules without a TCXO (#19)
Community apps zenobik (WM-BUS) and old386 (FISHNOID) in the app store
## Credits and open-source projects
Project Contribution
lr2021-re Alex Beal. Patch RAM programs for the LR2021's internal CPU that LakeShark runs on the radio: the on-chip FFT waterfall, the band sweep and the LoRa scanner. Our on-chip down-conversion is built with his ARC toolchain and loader. Write-up. MIT
Semtech LR20xx driver Semtech. The LR2021 Patch RAM image used by the bench build's radio probes. Clear BSD
rtl-sdr / librtlsdr Osmocom. RTL-SDR driver foundation. GPL-2.0+
xtrsdr XTR1984. ESP32-optimized librtlsdr implementation, essential to this project
OP25 Pavel Yazev's fixed-point imbe_vocoder. Experimental Phase II work by Max H. Parke, Graham J. Norbury and contributors. GPL-3.0+
libmodes / dump1090 Thomas Watson and Salvatore Sanfilippo. Mode S decoder lineage. BSD-2-Clause
ADS-B Scope John Stockdale and Off by One, Inc. Original implementation and single-frame CPR reference
DSD / dsd-fme szechyjs and lwvmobile. P25 symbol and framing foundations. ISC-style notices
mbelib szechyjs. Fallback vocoder. ISC
ESP-IDF Espressif. Embedded development framework
LILYGO device drivers T-Display P4 and MIX-RF hardware drivers, wiring and power examples
MeshCore Scott Powell / Ripple Radios and contributors. Mesh radio stack
CartoTUI / ZeroMesh libcarto rendering and embedded PMTiles reader
PMTiles Protomaps. Seekable, single-file offline map storage
OpenStreetMap Open map data. ODbL
Flipper Zero firmware Flipper Devices and contributors. Control-head platform and Crypto1 helpers
DejaVu Interface fonts
Waveshare ESP32-P4 board support and hardware examples
The field-map design drew on [Cardputer offgrid map](https://github.com/yuiseki/m5-cardputer-offgrid-tiny-map) by yuiseki and [HikePod](https://github.com/nongxl/HikePod) by nongxl. No source code was copied from either.

Open source. Built for experimentation.
